questions.stem: A patient stable on lithium starts daily ibuprofen and develops a coarse tremor and diarrhea. Why?

options.text: This is a normal lithium start-up effect

questions.explanation: B is correct: daily ibuprofen raised the lithium level, causing early toxicity. A is the opposite. C is a long-term antipsychotic effect. D ignores the new drug.

questions.stem: Which raise lithium levels? Select all that apply.

options.text: Drinking extra water with normal salt intake
Ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory pain relievers

questions.explanation: A, B, D, and E are correct: anything that makes the kidneys hold on to lithium raises the level. C is not taught as raising lithium.

questions.stem: A lithium patient starts hydrochlorothiazide. What happens to the lithium level?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the kidneys hold on to more lithium, so the level goes up. A and B are wrong for a thiazide. C is not a real effect.

questions.stem: Shortly after starting haloperidol, a patient has a sudden spasm of the neck. What treatment is taught?
questions.explanation: B is correct: acute dystonia is treated with diphenhydramine or benztropine. A treats tardive dyskinesia. C and D are not treatments for dystonia.

questions.stem: Which are metabolic effects of second-generation antipsychotics? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct: weight gain, high blood sugar, and high cholesterol, worst with olanzapine and clozapine. D and E are the opposite of what these drugs cause.

questions.stem: Which second-generation antipsychotics carry the highest metabolic risk?
questions.explanation: A is correct: olanzapine and clozapine are the worst. B and C list lower-risk drugs. D includes haloperidol, a first-generation drug known for movement effects.

questions.stem: Which statements about clozapine are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: It can cause seizures and severe constipation
No blood tests are needed anymore
The special safety program was removed in June 2025
Neutrophil counts are still checked per the label

questions.explanation: A, C, D, and E are correct as taught. B is wrong: no program does not mean no blood tests.

questions.stem: All antipsychotics carry a boxed warning for which group?
questions.explanation: D is correct: there is a higher risk of death in older adults with dementia-related psychosis. A, B, and C are not the groups in this boxed warning.

questions.stem: A patient in week 5 of clozapine has a fever and a sore throat. What is the best first action?

options.text: Check the absolute neutrophil count now
Wait for the next scheduled lab

questions.explanation: A is correct: fever or sore throat on clozapine can mean severe neutropenia, so check the count now and hold the drug if it is low. B delays a dangerous problem. C and D do not address it.
